title: Addition stories
examples: Teacher, how do I show this with numbers?
Can you show me another story problem?

explain.say: Look at this story. We have two apples. Then we get three more apples. How many apples altogether?
We can count them all together. One, two, three, four, five. So, two plus three equals five.
Another way is counting on. Start at three. Then count on two fingers. Three, four. So, three plus two equals five.
We can write this story as a number sentence. It shows the math problem. Two plus three equals five.

faq.a: It means putting groups together to find a total amount. You are joining two separate amounts into one group.
asks: How do I put things together?

faq.q: Is counting on the same as adding?
faq.a: Yes, counting on is a quick way to add numbers. You start at one number and count up by the other number.
asks: Can I count on for addition?
Is counting on a math trick?

faq.q: Why do I write a number sentence?
faq.a: A number sentence is just a way to write down the math problem you solved. It uses numbers and signs like plus and equals.
asks: How do I write the problem?

faq.q: What if the story has three groups?
faq.a: You can keep adding them one by one. You can write it like two plus three plus one equals six.
asks: Can I add more than two numbers?
What if there are three groups?

faq.q: Do I always need to use plus when combining?
faq.a: Yes, when you are putting things together, you use the plus sign. It means you are joining the groups.
asks: What sign do I use for joining?
Should I use plus or minus?

facts: Addition means putting groups together to find a total.
You can use your fingers to help you count when adding.
The plus sign means you are combining amounts.
An equals sign shows the total answer to the problem.

quiz.say: I had three red cars and two blue cars. How many cars altogether?
quiz.why: You put the three and the two together to count the total, which is five.

wrong.0: This is wrong because you added the numbers twice, which is too many.
wrong.1: This is wrong because you only counted the first group of cars.
wrong.3: This is wrong because you need to count all the cars, not just take away.

quiz.say: If you count on from four and add three more, what is the answer?
quiz.why: Start at four and count up three times: five, six, seven. The total is seven.

wrong.0: This is wrong because you forgot to count on the extra numbers.
wrong.2: This is wrong because you only counted one number up.
wrong.3: This is wrong because you added the numbers together too many times.

quiz.say: The story 'Five more balloons joined three balloons' can be written as:
quiz.why: The story means you are combining five balloons and three balloons to get a total of eight.

wrong.0: This is wrong because you put the numbers next to each other without an operation.
wrong.1: This is wrong because it does not show the action of combining the two groups.
wrong.3: This is wrong because you subtracted the numbers instead of adding them.
